newsitem.title: USA: Western Gas boosting East Texas capacity.
newsitem.headline: Western Gas boosting East Texas capacity.

text.p: Western Gas Resources Inc said Wednesday it has contracted to process additional East Texas sour natural gas and is expanding the capacity of a natural gas processing plant under construction near Bethel, Texas.

The company said it signed a long-term gathering and treating agreement with Broughton Associates Joint Venture covering all of Broughton's interests in the Cotton Valley Lime Formation and other sour gas formations within the Cotton Valley Pinnacle Reef trend in East Texas.
The agreement covers some 270,000 acres of undedicated interests in four counties of Texas.

Broughton has significant interests in six wells, of which three are currently capable of producing 52 million cubic feet per day, and plans to drill or participate in an additional 18 exploratory wells in the trend by the end of 1997.
Western said it already has long-term gathering and treating agreements in place with five producers in the trend, encompassing a leased-acreage dedication in excess of 500,000 acres.
The company said the sour-gas treating facility its Pinnacle Gas Treating Inc subsidiary is constructing near Bethel can treat up to 350 million cubic feet daily.
Producers have reserved 225 million cubic feet per day of firm capacity under fee-based contracts for gathering and treating services, Western said.
The company is expanding the planned gathering system serving the plant and now expects the plant's total capacity to be available in May, spokesman Ron Wirth said.
In September, Western Gas said 200 million cubic feet per day of capacity was expected to be available in April.

It said the expanded facilities are expected to cost approximately $62 million, an increase of $27 million from the $35 million announced in September. The initial phase will be financed using available credit under the company's revolving credit facility and with the funds received from a planned equity offering.
Western said it will extend the original 45-mile, 20-inch trunk line 30 miles further south and will increase the diameter of the first 30-mile segment of the line from 20 inches to 24 inches.
It is the larger pipe being used in the initial segment that allows the plant to come on line with a larger processing capacity, Wirth explained.
The company said it plans to expand trunk lines to the north and east as dedicated acreage is developed.

Western Gas said it continues to negotiate with other producers active in the trend. Should the current producers under contract, or others, require additional capacity, the company intends to expand the facilities in stages to accommodate new discoveries as they are completed.
